findings.finding: The Snow Country description reaches the 57th parallel and uses Nass/Kispiox watershed limits and the Alaska boundary. A same-named present LHA, or its name alone, cannot settle that extent.
Stikine’s legal perimeter uses the 56th parallel as one starting reference and a sequence of river watershed divides, continuing to the provincial boundary. It is not a rectangular latitude band.
The 2001 description includes dated Vancouver/Richmond municipal boundaries plus Greater Vancouver Electoral Areas A and B. A union of today’s municipal polygons alone is incomplete evidence.
findings.heading: Vancouver/Richmond Health Board Area

notes: Seeds are manually assigned from the printed council-map legend; duplicated printed labels identify mainland/island components for Campbell River/Nootka and Mount Waddington.
Central Coast’s printed number is offshore; the seed instead uses a point inside its filled mainland component. Its coastal island components are explicitly assigned by source drawing index.
The raster network closes only local source-stroke gaps. No modern administrative edges participate in tracing.
Coastal and tiny island membership remains generalized; the result is an estimated source drawing, not legal cadastral reconstruction.

limitations: All 52 administrative map labels now have an explicit working geometry; this does not verify their legal limits.
The 20 statistical illustrations are modern-LHA aggregates, kept separate from the 1995 legal board definitions.
Best estimates mix documented modern proxies with source-drawn approximations. Their uncertain edges can overlap; they are not a certified partition.

Drawing comparisons retain the full traced source footprint without modern-land clipping. Source-drawn best estimates alone are clipped for land display; historical marine jurisdiction remains unresolved.
Current municipalities, regional districts and school districts are similarity-screening references, not automatic substitutes for their historical versions.
